discovery_basis: Candidates were derived after the official ExtinctZoo YouTube market-pass report documented a gap: specific evidence-led reversals with original visual proof, rather than another generic deadliest/largest/strangest compilation.
source_policy: Primary papers and official journal pages are research evidence only. Journal figures, source photos, competitor thumbnails, footage, music, and narration are not production assets. Unknown or pending asset rights block production.

ideas.promise: What can one 465-million-year-old trilobite's preserved last meal reveal about how it digested food?
ideas.working_title: The Trilobite That Still Had Its Last Meal
ideas.topic_type: Ordovician fossil gut contents and physiology
ideas.market_gap_fit: A concrete internal fossil clue and a physiology reversal; not a generic strange-creature list or period superlative.

primary_evidence.citation: Kraft et al., Uniquely preserved gut contents illuminate trilobite palaeophysiology, Nature 2023
verified_claims: Ordovician Bohemolichas incola from approximately 465 Ma
complete itemized gut contents
3D synchrotron microtomography
partly fragmented calcareous shells
neutral or alkaline gut inference
scavengers avoided the gut
limitations: diet and physiology are inferences from preserved contents and taphonomy
do not generalize to every trilobite

observed: articulated exoskeleton and preserved axial gut fill as described by the paper
derived: a meal-to-physiology narrative built from the authors' interpretation
must_not_claim: that a pH value was directly measured in the living animal
that the specimen proves a universal trilobite diet

visual_proof_plan: Original side-view trilobite outline with the gut corridor highlighted.
Native cutaway animation showing shell fragments entering the gut and the evidence/inference boundary.
Original locality and time map; no reproduction of the Nature figure.
A final uncertainty card distinguishes scan observation from physiological interpretation.

rights_plan.allowed_path: Create original diagrams from cited facts; use no journal image, scan, specimen photograph, or third-party paleoart unless separately licensed.
blockers: Any direct reuse of Nature figures or scan render requires permission or a separately verified license.

feasibility_notes: Single central specimen gives a clean long-form arc
micro-CT concept can be illustrated natively
specialist terms need careful on-screen glosses
saturation_and_safety: Do not title it as the deadliest, strangest, or first-ever trilobite story without scope
Do not imply the visual cutaway is an actual camera view of the living animal

ideas.promise: How can a 245-million-year-old marine reptile fossil show that its group could give birth to live young?
ideas.working_title: The Reptile That Was Pregnant When It Died
ideas.topic_type: Middle Triassic reproduction and live birth
ideas.market_gap_fit: One embedded embryo supplies the physical reversal; it avoids ExtinctZoo's period-by-period predator and familiar-landscape packages.

primary_evidence.citation: Liu et al., Live birth in an archosauromorph reptile, Nature Communications 2017
verified_claims: pregnant Dinocephalosaurus from approximately 245 Ma
embryo enclosed within the maternal body
evidence for live birth in Archosauromorpha
authors model genotypic sex determination
limitations: the conclusion rests on specimen position, morphology, and clade context
sex-determination model is not the same as directly observed chromosomes

observed: maternal specimen and associated embryo elements as described in the primary paper
measured_or_published: embryo-to-mother size comparison in the paper
derived: a reconstruction of why internal position argues against simple superposition
must_not_claim: that every archosauromorph gave live birth
that the fossil shows a complete birth event
that sex chromosomes were directly recovered from the fossil

visual_proof_plan: Original silhouette and rib-cage cutaway with the embryo position marked.
A staged alternative-explanations board: swallowed prey, superposition, or embryo, with evidence for and against each.
A restrained marine-reptile habitat map and timeline; no copied reconstruction art.
Use an explicit uncertainty label around the phylogenetic/sex-determination inference.

rights_plan.allowed_path: Draw original anatomical schematics and use only independently licensed or public-domain contextual maps.
blockers: Primary-paper figures and specimen photography remain unlicensed for production.

feasibility_notes: clear general-audience conflict with the crocodile/bird mental model
requires careful distinction between archosauromorphs and dinosaurs
saturation_and_safety: Avoid the generic 'dinosaurs gave birth' claim
do not reuse competitor amphibian-apex or marine-reptile artwork
do not imply the animal is a direct ancestor of modern birds or crocodiles

ideas.promise: How did scientists prove that fish were feeding on the deep-sea floor 130 million years ago without finding the fish?
ideas.working_title: The Deep-Sea Fish We Know Only From Its Feeding Marks
ideas.topic_type: Early Cretaceous abyssal fish trace fossils
ideas.market_gap_fit: Behavioral evidence and a missing-body-fossil puzzle; a mechanism story instead of a creature superlative.

primary_evidence.citation: M. et al., The earliest evidence of deep-sea vertebrates, PNAS 2023
verified_claims: fish-feeding traces in Lower Cretaceous abyssal plain deposits of northwest Italy
approximately 130 Ma
trails and pits consistent with modern demersal feeding
at least three fish species inferred
earliest robust evidence for vertebrate deep-seafloor colonization in the paper's comparison
limitations: No fish body fossil is identified in the trace assemblage
feeding modes use comparison with modern fish traces
earliest claim depends on the defined fossil record and dating

observed: trails, pits, sediment relationships, and biostratigraphic context described by the paper
measured_or_published: late Hauterivian to early Barremian age
derived: an animated inference from a trace to a feeding behavior
must_not_claim: that the deep sea was empty before this fossil
that all pits were made by one animal

visual_proof_plan: Original slab-to-trace animation showing a feeding trail and pit in cross-section.
Native bathymetric/tectonic map placing the Tethys abyssal plain in the Cretaceous.
Three alternative feeding mechanisms animated with the paper's scope labels.
A final body-fossil-versus-trace-fossil distinction card.

rights_plan.allowed_path: Redraw trace geometry and maps from cited measurements; do not reuse PNAS figure files or source video.
blockers: Exact trace dimensions and any source image reuse need a permissions/license check before production.

feasibility_notes: Excellent central mystery with no need for a precise animal reconstruction
trace morphology is visually legible if simplified
requires clear explanation of how ichnology supports behavior
saturation_and_safety: Do not market it as the first fish in the deep sea in an absolute sense
do not turn trace analogy into direct observation

ideas.promise: Can the inside of one 100-million-year-old humerus show that a platypus-like lifestyle is older than the animal's outward shape?
ideas.working_title: The Platypus Clue Hidden Inside One Fossil Bone
ideas.topic_type: Early Cretaceous monotreme bone microstructure and ecology
ideas.market_gap_fit: A familiar living animal anchors a hidden-microstructure reversal; it is not a largest/deadliest/strangest list.

primary_evidence.citation: Hand et al., Bone microstructure supports a Mesozoic origin for a semiaquatic burrowing lifestyle in monotremes, PNAS 2025
verified_claims: Kryoryctes cadburyi is known from an Early Cretaceous humerus
age approximately 108–103 Ma
whole-bone shape resembles echidnas more than platypus
cortical microstructure includes specializations found in semiaquatic mammals
authors infer a semiaquatic burrowing lifestyle
limitations: Only a single humerus is currently known for Kryoryctes
the lifestyle is a probabilistic comparative inference
the paper does not make the animal a direct modern platypus ancestor

observed: one humerus and its internal structure as described by the paper
derived: a bone-interior-to-lifestyle story using an original cross-section
must_not_claim: that the animal had a platypus bill
that a single bone proves all early monotremes were aquatic
that echidnas are simply failed platypuses

visual_proof_plan: Original humerus cross-section comparing cortex and medullary cavity, with labels for observation versus inference.
Native platypus/echidna lifestyle comparison using original silhouettes, not stock or paper art.
Time-tree animation showing stem-monotreme placement without claiming direct ancestry.
A probability/uncertainty card that preserves the paper's comparative nature.

rights_plan.allowed_path: Create original bone sections and silhouettes; independently verify any modern-animal reference asset license.
blockers: No source image or scan is cleared for output; the native diagram path must be used.

feasibility_notes: Single-bone visual is controllable and diagrammable
familiar platypus/echidna hook lowers specialist decoding
microstructure terminology needs a visual glossary
saturation_and_safety: Do not call it 'the first platypus'
retain the 56.7% style of probabilistic reasoning if that is the reported comparison

ideas.promise: What can a 293-million-year-old fossilized vomit ball reveal about the predator that made it?
ideas.working_title: The Fossilized Vomit That Revealed a Permian Food Web
ideas.topic_type: Early Permian terrestrial regurgitalite and trophic ecology
ideas.market_gap_fit: A single physical object supports a behavior/food-web reversal, while the unknown producer creates honest uncertainty.

primary_evidence.citation: Early Permian terrestrial apex predator regurgitalite indicates opportunistic feeding behaviour, Scientific Reports 2026
verified_claims: open-access paper published 2026-01-30
Bromacker locality in Thuringia
41-bone compact cluster
micro-CT, osteological, chemical, and taphonomic analyses
oldest terrestrial regurgitalite claim in the paper
possible producers include Dimetrodon teutonis or Tambacarnifex unguifalcatus
limitations: Producer is not identified to a single taxon
regurgitalite interpretation is based on combined taphonomic and chemical evidence
do not present the candidate predator as observed fact

observed: compact bone cluster and its reported anatomical/taphonomic features
derived: a food-web reconstruction bounded by the candidate producer list
must_not_claim: that Dimetrodon definitely vomited the specimen
that the animal ate every named taxon in one meal without qualification
that fossil vomit is common or fully understood

visual_proof_plan: Original 3D bone-cluster diagram with elements color-coded by taxon and confidence.
Native digestive-path animation contrasting faeces, stomach contents, and regurgitalite.
Bromacker food-web map with branching candidate predators rather than one asserted culprit.
Micro-CT/taphonomy explanation using original motion graphics, not the paper's images.

rights_plan.allowed_path: Use the open-access paper as a factual source and redraw all output visuals; verify any license before reusing a figure.
blockers: The article's specific figures and specimen images still require license review despite open-access status.

feasibility_notes: single specimen can support a 15–22 minute investigation
producer uncertainty gives a built-in final limitation
saturation_and_safety: Avoid graphic gore or a copied dinosaur-vomit gag
do not flatten regurgitation, coprolite, and gut contents into one category
do not use 'apex predator' as a universal fact when the producer is unresolved
